policy: retry 5xx plus exactly {429,408}; max 4 attempts; backoff cap 30s
bug_report: Our auth service got hammered after a bad deploy - the HTTP client kept retrying calls that had failed with 401 Unauthorized, repeating the same doomed request until accounts locked out. Retrying cannot help a request the server has definitively refused. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix the retry decision without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: stop the HTTP client from retrying non-transient failures
decision_rationale: During the incident the client retried every failed request, including 401s, and locked accounts. Policy: retry any 5xx, plus exactly 429 and 408 from the 4xx range - 429 because the upstream rate-limits in bursts and 408 because their edge times requests out; every other 4xx is permanent and must not be retried. At most 4 attempts total, and backoff sleeps cap at 30 seconds because the gateway LB kills idle connections at 32s - sleeping longer just burns a dead connection.
